newsitem.title: UK: Bank of England leaves interest rates unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Bank of England leaves interest rates unchanged.

text.p: The Bank of England operated at established rates in the British money market on Thursday, indicating it had left official interest rates unchanged at 6.0 percent.
Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Kenneth Clarke met Bank of England Governor Eddie George on Wednesday for their monthly monetary policy meeting.
The central bank bought 250 million pounds in a repo -- a sale and repurchase agreement -- at 5-31/32 percent, its established interest rate for this financial instrument.
The Bank, which advises Clarke on monetary policy, has publicly called for official rates to be increased from the present 6.0 percent to prevent inflation taking off again.

But in a radio interview earlier on Thursday, Clarke said the strong pound had helped to counter inflationary pressures, while December retail price data published on Thursday showed underlying annual inflation falling to 3.1 percent
"The big thing at the moment is the pound is very strong and that is very anti-inflationary," Clarke told the BBC. REUTE RFM
